summary.tldr: Requires the Minister of Health to develop and table a national framework on fetal alcohol spectrum disorder, with consultations, standards, and follow-up reporting.
what_it_does: Requires the Minister of Health to develop a national framework on fetal alcohol spectrum disorder.
Sets out what the framework must cover, including training for health and other professionals, research, information-sharing, national standards, and awareness of alcohol use during pregnancy.

Requires the minister to consult provincial and territorial governments, Indigenous communities and organizations, health and research groups, caregivers, self-advocates, and other relevant people or bodies.
Requires the minister to table the framework in Parliament within 18 months after the Act comes into force and publish it on the Department of Health website within 10 days.
Requires a second report within five years on what parts of the framework have been carried out, how effective they are, and why any parts were not implemented.
who_it_affects: People with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder
summary.background: The bill says the framework is meant to support Canadians with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder, their families and their caregivers. It gives the Minister of Health the job of developing it.
